Note::float_item¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

double Note::float_item() const

Extract One Float64 Lane Without Rounding It¶

float_item() copies the sole lane of a Float64 Note into a native double. It is the scalar host boundary for scores and other continuous results. The method performs no text formatting, decimal rounding, allocation, or dtype conversion; the returned value carries the stored IEEE 754 bits into ordinary C++ computation.

Like the other typed item accessors, it is cardinality-based. A defined Float64 Note is accepted whenever numel() == 1, whether its shape is [], [1], [1, 1], or [1, 1, 1]. Rank is retained on the source and is not part of the extraction test.

Finite values, signed zero, infinities, and NaNs pass through unchanged. A default stream may print fewer digits than are needed to expose the stored binary value; use max_digits10 when a round-trippable decimal rendering matters. NaN equality remains false under ordinary IEEE comparison, so use std::isnan() to inspect a returned NaN.

Only Float64 Notes are accepted. Int64 is not promoted, Bool is not mapped to zero or one, and text is not parsed. Defined empty Notes, multi-element Notes, and undefined handles are also rejected. Validation occurs before extraction, so no result is produced on failure.

Use float_item() once a pipeline has intentionally produced one score. Use reals() for a zero-copy span over multiple lanes.

Example 1: Rank Zero And A Rank-Three Singleton¶

const auto scalar = pluss::note::make(0.125);
const auto rank3 = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<double>{1.25}, std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{1, 1, 1});

std::cout << "scalar=" << scalar.float_item()
          << " rank3=" << rank3.float_item() << '\n';

Output¶

scalar=0.125 rank3=1.25

Example 2: Reveal Full Stored Precision¶

const auto value = pluss::note::make(1.0 / 10.0);
std::cout << std::setprecision(std::numeric_limits<double>::max_digits10)
          << "precision=" << value.float_item() << '\n';

Output¶

precision=0.10000000000000001

The longer decimal is not introduced by float_item(); it exposes the exact Float64 approximation that was already stored.

Example 3: Preserve IEEE Special Values¶

const auto negative_zero = pluss::note::make(-0.0).float_item();
const auto infinity = pluss::note::make(
    std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity()).float_item();
const auto nan = pluss::note::make(
    std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN()).float_item();

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "special=" << std::signbit(negative_zero) << ','
          << std::isinf(infinity) << ',' << std::isnan(nan) << '\n';

Output¶

special=true,true,true

Example 4: Cardinality Must Be Exactly One¶

auto report = [](std::string_view label, const pluss::Note& value) {
  try { (void)value.float_item(); }
  catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << label << ": rejected\n"; }
};

report("float_item empty", pluss::note::make(std::vector<double>{}));
report("float_item multiple", pluss::note::make(std::vector<double>{0.25, 0.75}));

Output¶

float_item empty: rejected
float_item multiple: rejected

Example 5: Int64 Is Not Implicitly Promoted¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::int64_t{1}).float_item();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "float_item wrong dtype: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

float_item wrong dtype: rejected

Example 6: Undefined Has No Float64 Storage¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().float_item();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "float_item undefined: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

float_item undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • reals: borrow all native Float64 lanes.

  • is_float64: inspect the dtype without throwing.

  • numel: inspect cardinality before extraction.

  • scalar: borrow one Text or Bytes cell instead.
